parties.name: Labour
parties.summary: Labour commits to returning the NHS to the 18-week referral-to-treatment standard, delivering two million extra appointments per year through out-of-hours incentives, and pooling hospital resources to reduce waiting lists.

citations.quote: That means patients should expect to wait no longer than 18 weeks from referral for consultant-led treatment waiting lists and times and of non-urgent health conditions. This standard was achieved with the last Labour government and will be again under the next.

we will deliver an extra two million NHS operations, scans, and appointments every year; that is 40,000 more appointments every week. We will do this by incentivising staff to carry out additional appointments out of hours.

results.headline: Labour: mission is to build an NHS fit for the future
results.quote: Labour's mission is to build an NHS fit for the future.

parties.name: Conservative
parties.summary: The Conservatives pledge to return NHS performance to the standards set out in the NHS Constitution by the end of the next Parliament, backed by continued above-inflation spending increases and investment in technology and workforce expansion.

citations.quote: We are committed to accelerating the NHS's recovery from the pandemic, delivering safe and effective services and ongoing improvements in waiting times for primary, elective, cancer and emergency care. We will return performance to the levels set out in the NHS Constitution by the end of the next Parliament.

We will invest £3.4 billion in new technology to transform the NHS for staff and for patients. The NHS Productivity Plan will see NHS productivity grow by 1.9% a year from 2025-26 – unlocking £35 billion of cumulative savings by the end of the decade.

results.headline: Conservatives pledge 92,000 nurses and inflation-busting NHS spend
results.quote: Increase NHS spending above inflation every year, recruiting 92,000 more nurses and 28,000 more doctors.

parties.name: Liberal Democrats
parties.summary: The Liberal Democrats propose giving everyone the right to see a GP within seven days or within 24 hours if urgent, backed by recruiting 8,000 more GPs, and introduce a guarantee that 100% of cancer patients start treatment within 62 days of urgent referral.

citations.quote: Give everyone the right to see a GP within seven days, or within 24 hours if they urgently need to, with 8,000 more GPs to deliver on it.
Introducing a guarantee that 100% of patients will be able to start treatment within 62 days from urgent referral.

results.headline: Lib Dems pledge GP appointment within 7 days for everyone
results.quote: Give everyone the right to see a GP within seven days, or within 24 hours if they urgently need to, with 8,000 more GPs to deliver on it.

parties.name: SNP
parties.summary: The SNP calls on the UK Government to boost NHS England funding by at least £16 billion per year, which would generate additional consequential funding for NHS Scotland, and demands investment of £300 million to drive down waiting times in Scotland.
